title: Уряд спростив процедуру держконтролю імпортних ліків
content_c:
Уряд спростив окремі процедури державного контролю якості імпортованих лікарських засобів.
Як повідомляє міністерство охорони здоров'я, ці зміни дозволять прискорити постачання ліків до аптек і медзакладів та зменшити ризики перебоїв із їх постачанням в умовах війни.
"Відтепер уповноважена особа компанії-імпортера зможе самостійно перевіряти відповідність вантажу супровідним документам, проводити візуальний огляд упакувань з обов'язковою фотофіксацією. Також спрощено процедуру повторного ввезення тієї самої серії лікарського засобу", – уточнює МОЗ.
Відомство зазначає, що завдяки цим змінам компанії зможуть швидше проходити необхідні процедури та організовувати подальше постачання препаратів, уникаючи тривалого накопичення великих партій ліків на складах.

title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
content_c:
Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
- Published
A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history.
Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed.
The case is highly sensitive in Germany, one of Ukraine's closest allies since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, seven months before the attacks took place.
Extradited to Germany last year, Kuznetsov denies the charges, as does a second suspect who is fighting extradition from Croatia.
Kuznetsov became the first suspect to go on trial for the blasts on Wednesday morning, and a packed public gallery looked on as he entered the courtroom, appearing relaxed.
He even smiled at times, including during initial exchanges where he spoke to confirm personal details such as his name and place of birth.
He had previously only been identified by German prosecutors as Serhii K and pictured with his face blurred, but a court spokeswoman said he had now waived his anonymity.
Kuznetsov, 50, wore a pair of headphones and appeared to listen intently to a translation of proceedings in Ukrainian, as the prosecution read out the charges against him of ordering divers and an explosive expert to attack civilian infrastructure.
The defence outlined their case, telling the court that only circumstantial evidence had emerged in the four years since the Nord Stream blasts.
"[Prosecutors] made a thorough investigation of four years," Italian defence lawyer Nicola Canestrini told the BBC outside the courtroom. "They did not find one single witness, they did not find no forensics, no DNA, no fingerprints - nothing!"
Canestrini and his colleagues argued that as a soldier the defendant was bound to secrecy, and therefore he could not have a fair trial as he was unable to defend himself.
"Let's say he has an alibi, he was on another secret operation, how can you prove that if he's [not able] to tell us as defence attorneys where he was and which witnesses we could summon?"
Prosecutors argue the case falls under Germany's code of crimes against international law as a war crime, as an "attack by military means against civilian objects".
The defence told the court his extradition to Germany was flawed as no mention had been made at the time of the war crime allegation.
In the months after explosives destroyed three of the four gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea off the island of Bornholm on 26 September 2022, Western suspicion looked towards Moscow without directly apportioning blame.
Russia had already shut off the flow of gas to Germany in Nord Stream 1 weeks before the attack, and Nord Stream 2 had never been turned on. Berlin had frozen the multi-billion dollar project shortly before the invasion and there were reports of suspicious Russian naval movements before the blasts.
As investigators from Sweden, Denmark and Germany tried to find out who carried out the attack, Russia's Vladimir Putin accused the US and its UK allies, blaming "the Anglo-Saxons" - which they denied.
Eventually, after Denmark and Sweden shut down their inquiries, German prosecutors focused on a group of deep-sea divers who had rented a yacht called the Andromeda in the northern German port of Rostock.
They said later that "traces of subsea explosives were found in the samples taken from the boat".
Despite the strain on relations with Kyiv, German prosecutors pressed ahead with the case, and in January 2025 the German federal court of justice ruled that it fell within German territorial jurisdiction, external and prosecutors had a responsibility to act as it involved "undermining [Germany's] internal security".
Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky has always maintained that Ukraine had "nothing to do with [the Nord Stream blasts]", although in their indictment German prosecutors allege the saboteurs conceived the plot "acting by order of Ukrainian state agencies".
- Nord Stream trial: How German police followed the evidence - to Ukraine 
  - Published5 days ago
The case has highlighted differences of opinion on the trial in Kyiv and Berlin.
Oleksandr Merezhko, who chairs the Foreign Affairs Committee in the Ukrainian parliament, points out that the blasts took place during a time of war with Russia and "Nord Stream 2 was nothing but a tool used by Russia in order to get prepared for the war".
He told the BBC they had no confirmation of the German account: "It's one of the versions."
However, Stefan Meister, of the German Council on Foreign Relations, says successive chancellors in Berlin have done their best to remove the politics from the case.
"They tried to make not a big story out of it, not to give it too much attention, to give it to the institutions, to the judiciary that they will deal with it. This is not a political case. So they tried to depoliticise it," he explained.
In August 2025, Kuznetsov was arrested after checking into a hotel near the Italian Adriatic resort of Rimini, by police acting under a European arrest warrant issued by federal prosecutors in Germany.
After several weeks of court battles fighting extradition, when his surname emerged in court documents, Kuznetsov was transferred to Germany late last year.
German prosecutors allege that in 2022 he was a serving officer in the Ukrainian army, external, and he had led a group of professional divers, a boat captain and an explosives expert.
While his legal fight was going on in Italy, another Ukrainian man called Volodymyr Zhuravlov successfully challenged Germany's extradition bid in a Polish court.
In a ruling very different from Italy's Supreme Court, the Polish judge ordered Zhuravlov's release in October 2025, stating that the attack on the pipelines was not unlawful, and if Ukraine had organised an armed mission it was "justified, rational and just".
Although he was released by the court in Warsaw, he was arrested last August in Croatia on suspicion of being a suspect who "participated in the dives necessary" for the sabotage.
Last month, Croatia approved his extradition, although it is not clear when that will happen, and if his case could become part of the Hamburg trial.
Despite the difficult nature of the case for Kyiv and Berlin, Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko does not believe it will spoil relations as "it's in the best national interests of Germany to continue to support us".

title: Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police
content_c:
Tens of thousands of students have taken to the streets of Tirana, the Albanian capital, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption.
Police responded with water cannon and teargas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned bins and smashed the fronts of local businesses. A branch of Raiffeisen Bank near the education ministry also caught fire.
Authorities said 23 police officers and six other people were being treated for injuries and that 35 people had been detained.
President Bajram Begaj condemned the violence and appealed for calm, adding: “The constitution and the law must remain the boundaries for everyone, without exception.”
The protests are the most violent outburst yet against Edi Rama, the prime minister, who won a fourth term in office in May last year but has since faced growing discontent at perceived graft surrounding top officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures as unpalatable alternatives.
The unrest caps a summer of peaceful protests against Rama, triggered by the proposed development of a luxury resort along Albania’s pristine southern coast backed by Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, which has been caught up in legal disputes.
“This is a revolution. We are tired of peaceful protests. We will not stop until Rama resigns,” said Lora, a student who declined to give her last name as she threw rocks at the police.
Others chanted “resignation” and “police of crime”.
Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, a lack of financial support and employment prospects after graduation.
The unrest is part of a broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged weeks of protests and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education.
Albanian media reported that Wednesday’s protests had spread to universities at Elbasan and Shkodër.
The government condemned the violence.
Albana Koçiu, the deputy prime minister of Albania, said on Facebook: “Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road. I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: distance yourself from violence and vandalism!”
The police issued a statement calling for calm. “Any person who uses violence, burns or destroys property, or attacks police officers, bears individual responsibility and will face the law, in accordance with the offences committed,” they said.
Meanwhile, the EU, which the Balkan nation aspires to join, voiced concern over what it called the “violent escalation at the protest in Tirana”.
A statement by the EU delegation in Tirana said: “We take note of the allegations of excessive violence by the police against protesters and journalists,”
Calling for a prompt investigation, the delegation encouraged “all sides to de-escalate the tension”.

title: Germany news: Merz attacks extremes for fueling division
content_c:
Germany news: Merz attacks extremes for fueling division
Published October 14, 2026last updated October 14, 2026
What you need to know
These updates have been closed.
Here is a roundup of all the headlines across Germany from Wednesday, October 14:
- Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and socialist Left Party of fueling division and exploiting discontent for political gain
- The AfD leads national polls, while the Left Party has emerged as Berlin's largest party
- A man has gone on trial accused of playing a role in the 2022 explosion at the Nord Stream gas pipelines
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click hereto add DW as a Preferred Source on Google
Talks on forming Berlin coalition restart after antisemitism agreement with far-left party
Exploratory talks between The Left Party,the Greens and the Social Democrats (SPD) to form a coalition government in the city state of Berlin are set to continue after the trio agreed on the details of including opposition to antisemitism in a coalition agreement.
The breakdown in the talks can be traced back to concerns about the often highly critical stance on Israel adopted by some members of The Left Party.
Last Thursday, the three parties had signed a "binding" charter against antisemitism, while reiterating support for "Israel's right to exist."
These were preconditions from Greens and SPD for launching initial talks with The Left after state elections put the far-left party on top with 25.7% of the vote.
However, exploratory talks stalled on Tuesday after the lead candidates from the SPD and Greens said they needed "to assess whether our agreement from last week still stands."
The Greens' lead candidate, Werner Graf, and the SPD's Steffen Krach said The Left had "other arrangements within its group."
By Wednesday, The Left's parliamentary group leader, Elif Eralp, confirmed it would include the joint declaration in the coalition agreement if a government is formed.
"We met the Greens and SPD today and had a good and open conversation. We agreed that the misunderstandings between us have been cleared up," Eralp said.
"The leaders of all three parties stand behind the Berlin agreement," she added.
The SPD's Krach said it was important to make sure the agreement was clear, adding, "The Left Party's leadership has now confirmed that to us again."
The exploratory talks are to resume soon.
"From tomorrow we will meet again with the Greens and SPD to discuss the central challenges of our wonderful city," Eralp announced.
Two men violently free prisoner in Essen while he was out on a doctor's visit
Police have launched a major search in the western city of Essen after two masked men attacked prison officers taking an inmate to a doctor's appointment and freed him.
They overpowered and tied up the prison staff in the building lobby leading into the doctor's office on the Kennedyplatz in the city center, shortly before 1 p.m. local time (11 a.m. UTC).
The assailants and the inmate then split up and fled in different directions using e-scooters, police said. The prisoner was serving a custodial sentence for drug offenses and assault charges.
"The 34-year-old inmate with German citizenship and the two men suspected of freeing him are on the run. Police are searching for the men with numerous officers and has published a photo of the prisoner," Essen police wrote in a statement.
Police warned that it "could not be ruled out" that the suspects were armed, and asked anybody who thought they saw them not to approach or speak to them, but to call the emergency services immediately.
The operation also briefly involved a bomb scare that turned out to be a false alarm. Specialists deployed after a call from a concerned member of the public but it transpired the item was a wooden mock hand grenade.
Police did not immediately comment on whether the prisons officers accompanying the prisoner sustained injuries in the attack. 
 
Nord Stream trial draws supporters and media attention
There is huge interest in this court case. No sooner had the court doors opened at 07:30 local time in Hamburg than the first journalists, observers and protesters began arriving.
A small pro-Ukraine protest held up a banner saying, "Russia is a terrorist." One participant from Germany told me they wanted to remind the world of "the war crimes taking place against the Ukrainian people."
Inside, a Ukrainian student told DW that he and others had made the journey from Kyiv to show support for the defendant, Serhii Kuznietsov.
"Serhii Kuznietsov is a hero," the student said. In the eyes of the German prosecutors, it is another matter. They accuse him of carrying out a war crime. If found guilty of his part in the gas pipeline bombing, Kuznietsov faces a lengthy prison sentence.
Nord Stream defendant's lawyers challenge war crime charge
Lawyers for the Ukrainian man accused of organizing the Nord Stream pipeline attack have challenged the evidence and the war crime charge as his trial opened in Hamburg.
Serhii Kuznietsov, a 50-year-old former Ukrainian special forces officer, is accused of planning and supervising the September 2022 sabotage. Prosecutors say the attack targeted civilian infrastructure using prohibited methods of warfare.
Defense lawyer Jes Meyer-Lohkamp said there were no fingerprints, DNA traces or witness statements placing his client aboard the Andromeda, the yacht allegedly used in the operation.
Prosecutors allege Serhii Kuznietsov boarded the vessel on the German island of Rügen with six accomplices: a skipper, an explosives expert and four divers. The group allegedly attached four explosive devices fitted with timers to the pipelines.
His lawyers argued that Russia used the pipelines as a weapon of economic pressure, making them a legitimate target. They also said Italy had approved his extradition on sabotage allegations, rather than a war crime charge, and sought dismissal of the case.
The defense sought to have the case dismissed, also arguing that military secrecy obligations prevented Serhii K. from discussing potentially exonerating evidence, even with his lawyers.
The explosions ruptured three of the system's four pipelines near Denmark's Bornholm island. Russia had already halted supplies through Nord Stream 1, while Nord Stream 2 had never entered service.
Wadephul warns against economic 'gifts' to Russia
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has urged allies to maintain pressure on Russia following attacks on civilian ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.
"Gifts embolden Putin to continue on his course. Only firmness creates a willingness to talk," he said after meeting his Bulgarian counterpart in Berlin. He did not explicitly mention US President Donald Trump's recent diesel supply deal with Russia.
Wadephul said Europe must end its dependence on Russian energy to sustain economic pressure on Moscow.
He also urged Russia to agree to a ceasefire covering grain shipments, warning that further attacks threatened people facing hunger, particularly in Africa.
Fat-fingered cockpit error likely triggered Nuremberg hijack alert
A pilot's apparent mistake when entering a transponder code triggered the hijack alert that led to a major police operation at Nuremberg airport, German police said.
Investigators believe the pilot intended to report a radio failure but accidentally entered 7500, the code signaling a hijacking.
The Boeing 737-800's radio was defective, leaving the crew unreachable after takeoff from the Greek island of Corfu, police said.
Police spokesperson Michael Petzold said the pilot apparently did not realize the mistake. The pilot is not under investigation because police believe he acted unintentionally.
Military aircraft accompanied the plane in Croatian airspace, and Austrian interceptors were alerted. Two German Eurofighters then escorted it to Nuremberg.
A police team trained to negotiate with hijackers and a Bavarian support unit were deployed at the airport during the alert.
Officers had less than an hour between the emergency signal and landing to prepare, Petzold said. Police later gave the all-clear.
Lufthansa wins bid for stake in Portugal's TAP
Germany's Lufthansa has won the contest to buy a 44.9% stake in TAP Air Portugal with an offer of €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion), Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro said.
Lufthansa beat rival Air France-KLM after months of efforts to privatize the state-rescued airline, Montenegro told journalists following a cabinet meeting.
Social justice and Christian references: DW's Berlin bureau chief weighs in on Merz's speech
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's overriding message was one of justice, especially between generations.
That was for the home crowd, trying to explain the governing coalition's reform plans of the social systems. Interestingly he also sprinkled in some Christian references, something he seems to be doing more recently.
Most likely the German chancellor is trying to show more empathy and a more positive vision of the future.
His own conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party colleagues have increasingly been demanding this after losses in three state elections this fall.
Merz warns of growing injustice between generations
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has warned that Germany faces a growing gap in fairness between generations unless it undertakes major reforms of its social security systems.
"A justice gap has opened up between the generations in our country, and this gap will grow unless we act," Merz told the Bundestag.
He said children and young people risked being forced to shoulder a greater burden than could reasonably be justified under principles of fairness.
Merz acknowledged that successive governments had paid insufficient attention to the long-term consequences of their decisions, explicitly including governments led by his own center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
The chancellor said his government had developed a broad reform program covering pensions, care, the labor market, economic competitiveness and the modernization of the state.
He argued that justice should mean equal opportunities, fair rewards for achievement and fairness between generations, rather than redistribution at the expense of those contributing to the economy.
Merz said the reforms were necessary to preserve Germany's prosperity and ensure that younger generations were not left carrying an unfair share of the costs.
Merz accuses political extremes of seeking chaos
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has accused political forces on the far left and far right of deliberately dividing society, spreading disinformation and downplaying the threat posed by Russia.
Speaking in the Bundestag, Merz said he could not understand why politicians at both ends of the political spectrum continued to minimize Russian aggression.
"One gets the impression that you want chaos because you hope to gain political advantage from it," he told lawmakers.
Merz warned that extremism was increasingly making its presence felt in Germany's national and regional parliaments, as well as everyday life.
However, he acknowledged that extremist movements could draw support from legitimate dissatisfaction and feelings of injustice, arguing that constructive political action was the only effective response.
"Justice for us does not come through the exclusion of minorities," Merz said, calling for policies that promote equal opportunities and fairness between generations.
He contrasted what he described as the destructive politics of division and exclusion with the responsibility of democratic parties to address genuine grievances and govern for everyone in Germany.
WATCH: Merz addresses Bundestag before crucial EU summit
Merz says Ukraine aid does not come at welfare's expense
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has rejected accusations from the far right and far left that support for Ukraine comes at the expense of social spending.
"Not a single euro is missing from social spending," he told parliament, speaking ahead of an EU summit in Brussels.
Merz said an exemption from Germany's constitutional borrowing limits allows spending on defense and assistance for Ukraine to be financed through additional credit.
He accused the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the socialist Left Party of seeking to divide Germany

What you need to know
These updates have been closed.
Here is a roundup of all the headlines across Germany from Wednesday, October 14:
- Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and socialist Left Party of fueling division and exploiting discontent for political gain
- The AfD leads national polls, while the Left Party has emerged as Berlin's largest party
- A man has gone on trial accused of playing a role in the 2022 explosion at the Nord Stream gas pipelines
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click hereto add DW as a Preferred Source on Google
Talks on forming Berlin coalition restart after antisemitism agreement with far-left party
Exploratory talks between The Left Party,the Greens and the Social Democrats (SPD) to form a coalition government in the city state of Berlin are set to continue after the trio agreed on the details of including opposition to antisemitism in a coalition agreement.
The breakdown in the talks can be traced back to concerns about the often highly critical stance on Israel adopted by some members of The Left Party.
Last Thursday, the three parties had signed a "binding" charter against antisemitism, while reiterating support for "Israel's right to exist."
These were preconditions from Greens and SPD for launching initial talks with The Left after state elections put the far-left party on top with 25.7% of the vote.
However, exploratory talks stalled on Tuesday after the lead candidates from the SPD and Greens said they needed "to assess whether our agreement from last week still stands."
The Greens' lead candidate, Werner Graf, and the SPD's Steffen Krach said The Left had "other arrangements within its group."
By Wednesday, The Left's parliamentary group leader, Elif Eralp, confirmed it would include the joint declaration in the coalition agreement if a government is formed.
"We met the Greens and SPD today and had a good and open conversation. We agreed that the misunderstandings between us have been cleared up," Eralp said.
"The leaders of all three parties stand behind the Berlin agreement," she added.
The SPD's Krach said it was important to make sure the agreement was clear, adding, "The Left Party's leadership has now confirmed that to us again."
The exploratory talks are to resume soon.
"From tomorrow we will meet again with the Greens and SPD to discuss the central challenges of our wonderful city," Eralp announced.
Two men violently free prisoner in Essen while he was out on a doctor's visit
Police have launched a major search in the western city of Essen after two masked men attacked prison officers taking an inmate to a doctor's appointment and freed him.
They overpowered and tied up the prison staff in the building lobby leading into the doctor's office on the Kennedyplatz in the city center, shortly before 1 p.m. local time (11 a.m. UTC).
The assailants and the inmate then split up and fled in different directions using e-scooters, police said. The prisoner was serving a custodial sentence for drug offenses and assault charges.
"The 34-year-old inmate with German citizenship and the two men suspected of freeing him are on the run. Police are searching for the men with numerous officers and has published a photo of the prisoner," Essen police wrote in a statement.
Police warned that it "could not be ruled out" that the suspects were armed, and asked anybody who thought they saw them not to approach or speak to them, but to call the emergency services immediately.
The operation also briefly involved a bomb scare that turned out to be a false alarm. Specialists deployed after a call from a concerned member of the public but it transpired the item was a wooden mock hand grenade.
Police did not immediately comment on whether the prisons officers accompanying the prisoner sustained injuries in the attack. 
 
Nord Stream trial draws supporters and media attention
There is huge interest in this court case. No sooner had the court doors opened at 07:30 local time in Hamburg than the first journalists, observers and protesters began arriving.
A small pro-Ukraine protest held up a banner saying, "Russia is a terrorist." One participant from Germany told me they wanted to remind the world of "the war crimes taking place against the Ukrainian people."
Inside, a Ukrainian student told DW that he and others had made the journey from Kyiv to show support for the defendant, Serhii Kuznietsov.
"Serhii Kuznietsov is a hero," the student said. In the eyes of the German prosecutors, it is another matter. They accuse him of carrying out a war crime. If found guilty of his part in the gas pipeline bombing, Kuznietsov faces a lengthy prison sentence.
Nord Stream defendant's lawyers challenge war crime charge
Lawyers for the Ukrainian man accused of organizing the Nord Stream pipeline attack have challenged the evidence and the war crime charge as his trial opened in Hamburg.
Serhii Kuznietsov, a 50-year-old former Ukrainian special forces officer, is accused of planning and supervising the September 2022 sabotage. Prosecutors say the attack targeted civilian infrastructure using prohibited methods of warfare.
Defense lawyer Jes Meyer-Lohkamp said there were no fingerprints, DNA traces or witness statements placing his client aboard the Andromeda, the yacht allegedly used in the operation.
Prosecutors allege Serhii Kuznietsov boarded the vessel on the German island of Rügen with six accomplices: a skipper, an explosives expert and four divers. The group allegedly attached four explosive devices fitted with timers to the pipelines.
His lawyers argued that Russia used the pipelines as a weapon of economic pressure, making them a legitimate target. They also said Italy had approved his extradition on sabotage allegations, rather than a war crime charge, and sought dismissal of the case.
The defense sought to have the case dismissed, also arguing that military secrecy obligations prevented Serhii K. from discussing potentially exonerating evidence, even with his lawyers.
The explosions ruptured three of the system's four pipelines near Denmark's Bornholm island. Russia had already halted supplies through Nord Stream 1, while Nord Stream 2 had never entered service.
Wadephul warns against economic 'gifts' to Russia
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has urged allies to maintain pressure on Russia following attacks on civilian ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.
"Gifts embolden Putin to continue on his course. Only firmness creates a willingness to talk," he said after meeting his Bulgarian counterpart in Berlin. He did not explicitly mention US President Donald Trump's recent diesel supply deal with Russia.
Wadephul said Europe must end its dependence on Russian energy to sustain economic pressure on Moscow.
He also urged Russia to agree to a ceasefire covering grain shipments, warning that further attacks threatened people facing hunger, particularly in Africa.
Fat-fingered cockpit error likely triggered Nuremberg hijack alert
A pilot's apparent mistake when entering a transponder code triggered the hijack alert that led to a major police operation at Nuremberg airport, German police said.
Investigators believe the pilot intended to report a radio failure but accidentally entered 7500, the code signaling a hijacking.
The Boeing 737-800's radio was defective, leaving the crew unreachable after takeoff from the Greek island of Corfu, police said.
Police spokesperson Michael Petzold said the pilot apparently did not realize the mistake. The pilot is not under investigation because police believe he acted unintentionally.
Military aircraft accompanied the plane in Croatian airspace, and Austrian interceptors were alerted. Two German Eurofighters then escorted it to Nuremberg.
A police team trained to negotiate with hijackers and a Bavarian support unit were deployed at the airport during the alert.
Officers had less than an hour between the emergency signal and landing to prepare, Petzold said. Police later gave the all-clear.

Germany's Lufthansa has won the contest to buy a 44.9% stake in TAP Air Portugal with an offer of €1.2 billion ($1.3 billion), Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro said.
Lufthansa beat rival Air France-KLM after months of efforts to privatize the state-rescued airline, Montenegro told journalists following a cabinet meeting.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's overriding message was one of justice, especially between generations.

title: Nepal: Erneut schwere Überschwemmungen nach Unwettern
content_c:
Mitten im Wiederaufbau Neue Flut trifft Nepals Bergregionen
Erst vor wenigen Wochen erlebte Nepal eine verheerende Flutkatastrophe. Jetzt hat eine neue Flutwelle Häuser und Brücken mitgerissen. Rettungskräfte suchen nach Vermissten, ob es Tote gibt, ist bislang noch unklar.
Diesmal kam die Warnung rechtzeitig. Als am Sonntagmorgen der Fluss Budhi Gandaki im zentralnepalesischen Distrikt Gorkha anschwoll, konnten sich noch rechtzeitig Hunderte Bewohnerinnen und Bewohner und Touristinnen und Touristen in höher gelegene Gebiete retten.
Nach Angaben der nepalesischen Behörden war durch einen Erdrutsch Erde und Fels in den Fluss geschoben worden und bildete eine Art Staudamm. Als sich das Wasser seinen Weg durch die Blockade bahnte, schossen Schlamm und Geröll durch die Siedlungen flussabwärts.
Touristen waren zeitweise von der Außenwelt abgeschnitten
Fünf Menschen werden vermisst, ob es Tote gibt, ist bislang noch nicht bekannt. Die Flut hat Häuser, Felder und mehrere Brücken sowie Baustellen von drei Wasserkraftwerken beschädigt. Zeitweise waren mehr als 100 ausländische Trekkingtouristen von der Außenwelt abgeschnitten. Inzwischen ist der Wasserstand gesunken. Die Versorgung abgelegener Orte und die Suche nach den Vermissten gehen weiter.
Das betroffene Gebiet liegt nicht in den bereits im August verwüsteten Tälern. Diesmal traf es den Distrikt Gorkha, rund 100 Kilometer westlich von Kathmandu. Die damalige Katastrophe hatte vor allem Rasuwa und Nuwakot nahe der Grenze zu Tibet getroffen.
Viele Familien leben in den Bergregionen vom Tourismus
Für Gorkha kommt die Flut zur denkbar ungünstigsten Zeit. Oktober und November sind die Hauptsaison für Wanderungen im Himalaya. In den Bergregionen leben viele Familien von der Vermietung von Unterkünften, betreiben Restaurants oder arbeiten als Bergführer und Träger.
Nach der Katastrophe im August hatte die Regierung Touristen gebeten, ihre Reisen nicht pauschal abzusagen. Die meisten Ziele und Trekkingrouten seien geöffnet. Im jetzt betroffenen Manaslu-Gebiet sind jedoch erneut Wege unterbrochen und Brücken fortgerissen worden.
Fast 1.500 Menschen kamen bei der Flut im August ums Leben
Nepal hat sich von der Flut Ende August noch lange nicht erholt. Damals waren an der Grenze zwischen Tibet und Nepal gewaltige Mengen Fels und Gletschereis abgebrochen und in einen Gebirgsfluss gestürzt. Die ausgelöste Flutwelle riss ganze Orte mit sich. Mindestens 1.455 Menschen kamen ums Leben, mehr als 5.000 gelten noch als vermisst.
Tausende Häuser wurden beschädigt oder zerstört. In abgelegenen Tälern fehlen Straßen und Brücken, die Versorgung mit Trinkwasser und Strom ist vielerorts noch immer eingeschränkt. Viele Betroffene leben in provisorischen Unterkünften. Ob und wann sie zurückkehren können, wissen sie nicht.
Wiederaufbau kostet knapp fünf Milliarden US-Dollar
Anfang Oktober beendete die Regierung die Suche nach Überlebenden und die Bergung der Toten. Für viele Familien bleibt damit die Ungewissheit. Solange Vermisste nicht offiziell für tot erklärt werden, fehlen Angehörigen häufig notwendige Unterlagen für Entschädigungen, Versicherungen oder Erbschaften.
Die Regierung schätzt, dass der Wiederaufbau knapp fünf Milliarden US-Dollar kosten wird - etwa ein Zehntel der jährlichen Wirtschaftsleistung Nepals. Premierminister Balendra Shah fordert deshalb vor allem Zuschüsse statt weiterer Kredite.
Sein Argument: Nepal leide besonders stark unter dem Klimawandel, verursache aber nur einen sehr kleinen Teil der weltweiten Treibhausgasemissionen. Das Land müsse sich zusätzlich verschulden, um die Folgen dieser Katastrophen zu bewältigen. Das dürfe nicht sein.

title: "Они знали, что делали": Зеленский обвинил США в намеренном ограничении работы Starlink, а Маск кивнул на Трампа
content_c:
Президент Украины Владимир Зеленский считает, что США и SpaceX сознательно ограничили работу Starlink во время российского нападения на Украину. Это помешало задействовать часть дронов-перехватчиков, в результате чего погибли люди. В то же время Илон Маск заверил, что работу Starshield ("военного пакета" Starlink) контролирует Пентагон и президент США, а не его компания.
В интервью британскому телеведущему Пирсу Моргану Зеленский рассказал, что Starlink перестал работать около часа ночи. На вопрос, могли ли ограничения быть введены намеренно, президент ответил:
"Я уверен, что они знали, что делали. Абсолютно. Потому что это был час ночи. Час ночи".
Сознательное давление
Зеленский заявил, что за блокировкой Starlink стоят SpaceX и США. Он признал их право ограничивать работу системы, но напомнил, что украинские военные используют спутниковую связь не только для нанесения ударов по российским целям, но и для защиты от атак.
В частности, Starlink нужен дронам-перехватчикам, которые украинские военные применяют против реактивных "Шахедов".
"Речь идет о защите человеческих жизней. Поэтому люди погибли, поскольку удалось уничтожить недостаточное количество беспилотников. Не хватило перехватчиков, в частности перехватчиков с помощью Starlink, который не работал", — отметил Зеленский.
Президент связал ограничения Starlink с другими событиями той ночи — российскими ударами баллистическими ракетами и отсутствием заблаговременных предупреждений от партнеров о запусках ракет. По его мнению, все это было частью давления на Украину.
Что говорит Маск
Маск в ответ на пост бывшего министра обороны Михаила Федорова заявил, что Starshield принадлежит правительству США, которое и контролирует его работу. Ограничения скорости и использования системы, по словам бизнесмена, устанавливают американские военные, а окончательное решение остается за президентом США.
"Starlink — это коммерческая услуга, принадлежащая компании SpaceX и находящаяся под её контролем. Использование Starlink ограничивается гражданскими или оборонными целями и не может применяться для наступательных военных действий, поскольку это было бы неуместно для коммерческой компании", — написал Маск.
Федоров ранее сообщил, что Starlink в Украине снова начал работать во время движения со скоростью до 160 км/ч. Он поблагодарил Маска, но подчеркнул, что для украинской обороны необходимо полностью отменить ограничение скорости в Starshield.
Хронология событий
Утром 14 октября общественный деятель Сергей Стерненко сообщил, что терминалы Starlink переставали работать во время движения. Сначала связь пропадала на скорости свыше 160 км/ч, а впоследствии — уже при 60–70 км/ч.
Советник президента по технологическим направлениям обороны Сергей Бескрестнов с позывным "Флеш" пояснил, что SpaceX без предупреждения ввела скоростные ограничения для военного пакета Starshield, которые ранее действовали только для гражданских терминалов.
По словам Бескрестнова, из-за перебоев сорвались некоторые военные операции, возникли проблемы с логистикой и работой дронов-перехватчиков, которые используются против российских реактивных беспилотников.
Проблемы со Starlink возникли на фоне давления Вашингтона на Киев из-за ударов по российским нефтеперерабатывающим заводам. По данным СМИ, после объявления Дональдом Трампом "энергетического перемирия" представители его администрации требовали от украинских военных и чиновников прекратить эти атаки и угрожали последствиями.
Ранее Маск поддержал заявления Трампа, который обвиняет Украину в подорожании топлива из-за ударов по НПЗ РФ.
"Зеленский зашел слишком далеко", — написал он в своей социальной сети X.

title: Кількість загиблих унаслідок атаки на Кропивницький зросла до трьох – ОВА
content_c:
Кількість загиблих унаслідок масованої російської атаки на Кропивницький зросла до трьох, ще шестеро людей травмовані, повідомив начальник Кіровоградської обласної військової адміністрації Андрій Райкович.
"Ще одна сумна новина – стало відомо про третього загиблого в обласному центрі. Мої співчуття рідним", – написав він у телеграмі.
За його даними, п'ятеро травмованих перебувають у медичних закладах міста, ще один від госпіталізації відмовився.
Атака на область триває.
Як повідомлялося, внаслідок масованої російської атаки на Кропивницький загинули двоє людей, атака на область триває, повідомив начальник Кіровоградської обласної військової адміністрації Андрій Райкович.
Джерело: https://t.me/kirovogradskaODA/27666

title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
content_c:
Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
- Published
Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, 10 days after a businessman died of the virus after he had travelled to the East African nation from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The new patient, a 39-year-old man, is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill on Tuesday, Kenya's health ministry says.
The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.
Detecting his illness early had improved his chances of recovery and limited the chance of him passing the virus on to others, the ministry said, as it urged the public to "stay calm but vigilant".
"Both cases are linked, and there is no evidence of spread in the wider community," the ministry said.
"Kenya remains open, with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings", it added.
The 40-year-old Kenyan man who died on 5 October was diagnosed with Ebola shortly after being admitted to hospital in the capital, Nairobi.
A relative had taken him there shortly after picking him up at the airport. He had travelled from DR Congo, through Uganda to Kenya without his illness being detected.
Since his death, officials had determined that he had been in contact with 128 people - and since Tuesday 113 of them had been found, the health ministry said.
Of these, 108 were in quarantine in Kenya and tracing of the remaining 15 continued, it said.
More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.
The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.
"Anyone with fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pains, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding should seek care promptly at the nearest health facility," Kenya's health ministry said.
The current outbreak in DR Congo, which began in May, has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.
Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died.
However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the continent's leading public health agency, has reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements for the six weeks leading up to his death.
It revealed that he first started feeling unwell in DR Congo on 15 September - and showed how several opportunities to detect the infection were missed, including during several visits to Congolese medical facilities.
He then managed to travel through Uganda to Kenya - and was again not detected at airports screenings.
Health experts say it highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

title: Pope Leo’s recovery from lung cancer surgery ‘progressing as planned’
content_c:
Pope Leo’s recovery from a lung cancer operation is progressing as planned, his doctors have said, as the pontiff received good wishes from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles.
Leo, who had a cancerous mass removed from his right lung late on Tuesday, began walking in his hospital room after respiratory therapy on Wednesday. He was eating normally, his doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritoria said in a statement issued by the Vatican.
A blood test and chest X-ray showed “normal post-operative progress” and the results were “within the expected range for the type of procedure performed”, they said.
The operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital confirmed that Leo, 71, has the most common kind of lung cancer – adenocarcinoma. The Vatican has not yet disclosed the results of further tests to determine whether the cancer has spread and if more treatment will be needed.
The cancer diagnosis for Leo, who was elected as the first US-born leader of the Roman Catholic church in May 2025, has come as a shock.
In a rare moment of Vatican transparency, the pope announced during his angelus prayer on Sunday that doctors had found a small nodule on his lung during a checkup and that it was “well-contained” and had been detected early.
Messages have been sent from around the world. King Charles, who is also being treated for an undisclosed form of cancer, would write to Leo privately, a source told Agence France-Presse. Charles and Queen Camilla met the pope when they travelled to the Vatican in October last year.
Donald Trump, the US president, said: “I want to see Pope Leo get well. I just want to wish him well, get better fast.”
Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, wished Leo a full and swift recovery in a message posted on X and said the pontiff was “a source of hope and inspiration for billions around the world”.
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said he and his wife, Jeanette, were praying for Leo. The couple met the pontiff at the Vatican in May.
The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, wrote on X that Leo’s serenity and strength were an inspiration for all. “We hope for his full and speedy recovery,” she wrote.
Before the operation, all of Leo’s appointments until 20 October were cancelled. He went on a papal trip to France in September and is scheduled to go to South America in November for a 12-day trip covering 10 cities.

Donald Trump, the US president, said: “I want to see Pope Leo get well. I just want to wish him well, get better fast.”
Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, wished Leo a full and swift recovery in a message posted on X and said the pontiff was “a source of hope and inspiration for billions around the world”.
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said he and his wife, Jeanette, were praying for Leo. The couple met the pontiff at the Vatican in May.
The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, wrote on X that Leo’s serenity and strength were an inspiration for all. “We hope for his full and speedy recovery,” she wrote.
Before the operation, all of Leo’s appointments until 20 October were cancelled. He went on a papal trip to France in September and is scheduled to go to South America in November for a 12-day trip covering 10 cities.

title: Houthis launch fresh wave of missiles across Saudi Arabia
content_c:
Houthis launch fresh wave of missiles across Saudi Arabia
Published October 14, 2026last updated October 14, 2026
What you need to know
These updates have been closed.
Below, you can review headlines from the Saudi-Houthi conflict and elsewhere in the Middle East from Wednesday, October 14, 2026:
- Fire breaks out at Aramco headquarters in Dhahran
- Four injured because of debris in Saudi capital Riyadh
- Fuel facility in Sanaa hit by Saudi-led coalition forces
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google.
US military destroyed Iran-affiliated vessel in Gulf of Oman, CENTCOM says
US forces destroyed an Iran-affiliated vessel in the Gulf of Oman last week, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said on Wednesday.
CENTCOM said the vessel was conducting surveillance and targeting US Navy ships. The ship's crew members were safely removed from the vessel before the attack, the military command said.
Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has sharply decreased since the war in Iran broke out.
The strait, bordered by Iran, is key in connecting major oil producers to the rest of the world.
Houthis again claim to have targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport
A Houthi military spokesman said on Wednesday evening that the Iran-backed group had targeted Riyadh's international airport with a ballistic missile.
The comments came hours after the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a ballistic missile fired towards the capital, though it wasn't entirely clear if the two sides were talking about the same incident.
"Our armed forces were able to taget Khalid International Airport in the Saudi enemy's capital, Riyadh, with a ballistic missile, and the strike was precise and direct," Yahya Saree wrote on X.
The airport has come under repeated fire since an attack on Saturday that killed 12 people.
The Houthi spokesman Saree also claimed three other ballistic missile stikes in other areas "resulting in a large number of dead and wounded, as well as the disabling of several vehicles," saying they hit "enemy mobilization points."
Saudi authorities have not reported any deaths as a result of Houthi strikes on Wednesday.
Saudi Arabia postpones 'Six Kings Slam' tennis tournament
Saudi Arabia has postponed a high-profile exhibition tennis tournament that was scheduled to take place next week, as Houthi attacks on the country continue to create major security concerns.
The "Six Kings Slam" has been postponed until December 27-30, organizers said on Wednesday in a statement that went to impressive lengths not to refer to the conflict or potential security risks in any way.
"The decision reflects Riyadh Season's commitment to delivering sporting events to the highest standards, following an assessment of the organizational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament and their potential impact on the quality of the audience experience," organizers said.
The tournament was originally slated for October 21-24.
Carlos Alacaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien were originally scheduled to compete, after defending champion Jannik Sinner withdrew with an injury.
However doubts about the likelihood of the stars traveling to the tournament amid the current security situation were already rife.
The Six Kings Slam is a men-only exhibition tournament not a ranking event, but it's a high profile end-of-season competition streamed on Netflix whose large prize purse tends to attract the world's best players.
Other Saudi sporting events could in theory be in doubt, including the Saudi International golf tournament in Riyadh next month, and later the 2027 Asian Cup football competition.
This year's F1 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was canceled amid the war in Iran, even before Houthi military activity against Saudi Arabia specifically intensified. Jeddah is again on the 2027 calendar, scheduled for March 19-21.
Red Cross warns that Yemen's hospitals are at capacity
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has cautioned that Yemen's hospitals are finding it difficult to cope with the skyrocketing amount of war injuries as fighting intensifies across the country.
Small hospitals in front-line areas in Marib and Taiz are seeing some 700 casualties of the conflict in a single week, a far great number than their usual amount of patients.
"Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure," ICRC health coordinator Feras Abusamra said in a statement.
Only a handful of hospitals in Yemen are capable of handling intensive care patients, and even those lack many of the necessary supplies and medicines as other health facilities across the country.
At least 200,000 people have been displaced in the conflict, further complicating matters for Yemen's still-functional hospitals. Moreover, due to changing front lines on multiple fronts, international organizations say at least 800,000 people have become cut off from much-needed humanitarian aid.
Riyadh residents report explosions
Civilians in the Saudi capital Riyadh reported hearing an explosion above their city as the govenment claimed in intercepted a ballistic missile launched from Yemen.
The Houthis then claimed they had again struck Riyadh airport as well as an Aramco oil refinery, something Saudi authorities have not confirmed.
The increase in attacks on Saudi soil has increased pressure on Riyadh's allies, including the United States, to evaluate whether they should join the coalition against the Houthis more directly.
IMF warns attacks on Saudi could impact people "everywhere"
The recent attacks on Saudi Arabia could affect people adversely "everywhere," as conflict in the energy-rich region could lead to a range of economic concerns, International Monetary Fund (IMF) head Kristalina Georgieva said Wednesday.
The escalation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia has sparked fears of aggravating global crises that could impact global growth, with energy markets already disrputed due to the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US.
"The Saudi economy is important for the region and the world," IMF managing director Georgieva said at a news conference during the Annual Meetings of the Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.
"In that sense, these developments have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere," she said.
Aramco offices catches fire after suspected Houthi attack
Saudi Arabia said that an attack on the headquarters of oil state oil firm Aramco sparked a "limited fire."
The fire at the building at Aramco's complex in the eastern city of Dhahran resulted in no casualties or deaths, the country's Energy Ministry said.
A company source told the Reuters news agency that a ballistic missile struck the top floors of an office building.
The complex in Dhahran serves as a major operation for Aramco, which is the world's largest oil company.
Hours earlier, Saudi authorities said they had intercepted several missiles, including over the capital city Riyadh.
Several injured by fallen missile debris in Riyadh
Four people were injured as a result of falling debris following two intercepted Houthi missile attacks, Saudi authorities said.
According to the country's civil defense agency, two women, a man and a child were injured in the capital Riyadh, with 15 homes suffering damage.
This came after residents heard a powerful explosion in the Saudi capital, with an alert being sent to their phones warning of a "hostile aerial threat."
Saudi-led coalition strikes Sanaa fuel facility
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis struck targets in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa on Tuesday, Houthi-run broadcaster Al Masirah said.
Locals reported hearing strong explosions in the city hours after a coalition spokesperson urged people to leave the all-Suhaba fuel facility, which belongs to the Yemeni Oil Company, and a nearby site ahead of a strike.
According to a coalition spokesperson, the Houthis were using the facility for storing missiles and drones. The facility is located on a hill overlooking Sanaa.
The company said the storage facilities at the site were empty, with a strike not affecting oil reserves or supplies to residents.
Welcome to our coverage
We will be following all the latest updates from the escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen-based militant group, the Houthis.
The compound of energy company Aramco saw a fire break out, the Saudi Ministry of Energy said. Saudi authorities also reported four injuries as a result of missile debris falling over Riyadh.
Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen continued its strikes on Tuesday by targeting oil facilities west of capital Sanaa, the local Houthi-run broadcaster said.
Join us as we bring you the latest.
description: Both the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition carried out strikes targeting energy infrastructure. Four people were injured as a result of debris of intercepted missiles in Riyadh.

title: Iran-Krieg: Zwei Containerschiffe nach Beschuss in Straße von Hormus gesunken
content_c:
Umkämpfte Meerenge Containerschiffe nach Beschuss in Straße von Hormus gesunken
Die Straße von Hormus bleibt die wohl gefährlichste Schifffahrtsroute der Welt. Und zuletzt hat sich die Situation für Transporte durch die umkämpfte Meerenge noch einmal dramatisch verschärft. Das zeigen die Vorfälle rund um mehrere Schiffe, die in dem Gebiet angegriffen wurden.
Ein Containerschiff ist bei der Fahrt durch die Straße von Hormus gesunken. Das teilte die Hafenbehörde in Singapur mit. Demnach wurden die »GFS Pride« und ein weiteres in Singapur registriertes Schiff von unbekannten Geschossen getroffen, während sie die Meerenge passierten.
Die »GFS Pride« sei dabei beschädigt worden und habe Feuer gefangen. Inzwischen sei das Schiff gesunken. Die 21 Besatzungsmitglieder konnten rechtzeitig evakuiert werden, hieß es in der Mitteilung. Berichte über Verletzte gibt es demnach keine. Laut dem Schiffsortungsdienst Vesselfinder befand sich die »GFS Pride« auf dem Weg zum Hafen Fudschaira in den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten.
Das zweite angegriffene Schiff, die »GFS Giselle«, habe Schäden am Schiffsrumpf erlitten, aber mit eigenem Antrieb einen sicheren Hafen erreicht, so die Mitteilung weiter. Die 22 Besatzungsmitglieder seien in Sicherheit und unverletzt. Die Singapurer Behörde verurteilte die Angriffe als »unprovoziert, nicht zu rechtfertigen und Verstoß gegen internationales Recht«.
Auch die iranische Nachrichtenagentur Tasnim, die den Revolutionswächtern nahesteht, hatte über ein gesunkenes Containerschiff berichtet. Dieser Darstellung zufolge fuhr der Frachter in der Straße von Hormus auf eine Seemine. Nach iranischen Angaben waren 2500 Container geladen. Aufnahmen aus der Region zeigen Dutzende Container im Wasser.
Offenbar ist auch die »Cape Dao« gesunken
Der britische »Guardian« berichtet zudem , nur Stunden nach der »GFS Pride« sei auch das Containerschiff »Cape Dao« nahe der Straße von Hormus gesunken. Die »Cape Dao« unter der Flagge von Antigua und Barbuda war demnach bereits am 23. September von einem Geschoss getroffen und schwer beschädigt worden. Ein Mensch war damals ums Leben gekommen.
Irans Streitkräfte haben ihre Angriffe auf die Schifffahrt in der Straße von Hormus in den vergangenen Tagen intensiviert. Sie attackieren dabei in der Regel Tankschiffe und Frachter, die sich auf einer südlichen Route nahe der omanischen Küste befinden. Seit mehreren Monaten begleitet die US-Marine dort zivile Handelsschiffe, um den Handel mit Öl und Flüssiggas wieder zu ermöglichen. Teheran betrachtet die Route als »illegal« und fordert die Passage entlang der iranischen Küste.
Iran blockiert seit Beginn des Krieges Ende Februar mit Drohungen und Angriffen auf Schiffe den Verkehr weitestgehend. Auch das US-Militär hat wiederholt zivile iranische Schiffe attackiert. Die an ihrer engsten Stelle nur 35 bis 40 Kilometer breite Straße von Hormus ist im Irankrieg zum zentralen Konfliktpunkt zwischen Iran und den USA geworden.
description: Iran verschärft seine Angriffe in der Straße von Hormus. Gleich zwei Schiffe wurden beim Versuch der Durchfahrt versenkt. Ein weiteres konnte beschädigt aus der Gefahrenzone gebracht werden.

title: Haushaltsdebatte in Frankreich: Die politische Quadratur des Kreises
content_c:
Haushaltsdebatte in Frankreich Die politische Quadratur des Kreises
In Frankreich haben die Beratungen über den Haushalt begonnen. Angesichts hoher Schulden will Finanzminister Lescure deutlich sparen. Aber die Regierung hat keine eigene Mehrheit - und stößt auf Widerstand.
Der Rahmen wollte so gar nicht passen - gemessen an der politischen Bedeutung der Debatte. Zum Auftakt der Haushaltsberatungen stand Finanzminister Roland Lescure am späten Dienstagabend vor einem nahezu leeren Plenarsaal und versuchte die wenigen Anwesenden vom Ernst der Lage zu überzeugen: "2026 ist noch nicht vorbei - und das Jahr ist davon geprägt, dass sich Krisen häufen", sagte er. Man müsse unbedingt zu einem ausgeglichenen Haushalt zurückfinden. "Deshalb schlagen wir 2027 wieder den Sanierungskurs ein."
Finanziell steht Frankreich mit dem Rücken zur Wand: Die Schuldenquote liegt bei knapp 120 Prozent der Wirtschaftsleistung. Allein für Zinszahlungen auf Kredite sind im laufenden Haushalt fast 80 Milliarden Euro eingeplant.
"Wir dürfen uns damit nicht abfinden", mahnt Lescure. "Um zu verhindern, dass wir immer mehr Geld leihen müssen und um unsere Spielräume zu erhalten, gibt es nur einen Weg: unser Haushaltsdefizit zu reduzieren" - und zwar von aktuell 5,4 auf 5,0 Prozent der Wirtschaftsleistung.
Kürzungen in Höhe von 40 Milliarden Euro geplant
Dafür plant die Regierung in ihrem Haushaltsentwurf "Sanierungsmaßnahmen" in Höhe von gut 40 Milliarden Euro. Kürzen will sie bei Entwicklungshilfe und Beschäftigungspolitik, Renten und Wohnzuschüsse sollen nicht wie üblich an die Inflation angepasst werden.
Die Verteidigungsausgaben hingegen sollen deutlich steigen. Éric Coquerel von der linksradikalen Partei LFI ist Vorsitzender des Haushaltsausschusses. Er bezeichnete die Warnungen der Regierung als "Schwarzmalerei" und warf ihr vor, wirtschaftspolitisch gescheitert zu sein: "Diejenigen, die sagen, wir hätten kein Geld mehr, sind nicht in der Position, um Lektionen zu erteilen!"
Opposition sieht Scheitern der Regierung
Sie seien alle an ihren Versprechungen gescheitert, meint Coquerel: "Sie haben das Haushaltsdefizit nicht reduziert, die Arbeitslosigkeit steigt wieder und liegt bei gut acht Prozent." Diese Politik habe das Land kaputtgemacht.
Die Regierung steht vor einer fiskalischen Herkulesaufgabe. Und einem politischen Drahtseilakt. Denn in der Nationalversammlung hat sie keine eigene Mehrheit - und auf die Kompromissbereitschaft der Opposition kann sie wohl kaum zählen: ein halbes Jahr vor der Präsidentschaftswahl.
Sozialisten forderten Ablehnung noch vor Debatte
Im Laufe des Abends füllte sich der Plenarsaal in der Assemblée. Die Sozialisten hatten einen Antrag eingebracht, um den Budgetentwurf der Regierung abzulehnen, noch bevor die inhaltliche Debatte darüber überhaupt angefangen hatte.
Die Abgeordnete Estelle Mercier rechtfertigte den Schritt ihrer Fraktion: "Dieser Haushaltsentwurf zeichnet sich nicht durch Vernunft aus - sondern durch Ungerechtigkeit. Ein vernünftiges Haushaltsgesetz in einem Parlament ohne Mehrheit, in einem gespalteten Land müsste ein gerechtes sein. Es müsste eines sein, das alle an den Sparanstrengungen beteiligt, gemessen an ihren Fähigkeiten - und das dadurch kompromissfähig wäre."
Der Antrag scheiterte, die Budgetverhandlungen nehmen also ihren Lauf. Die Episode zeigt aber, wie groß der politische Druck auf die Regierung ist. Den letzten Haushalt konnte Regierungschef Sébastien Lecornu vor allem dank den Verhandlungen mit den Sozialisten durchs Parlament bringen - die jetzt aber auf Konfrontation gehen.
Le Pen denkt an ihre mögliche Präsidentschaft
Marine Le Pen verfolgt eine andere Strategie. Auf einer Veranstaltung von Politico sagte die Präsidentschaftskandidatin des rechtsnationalen Rassemblement National zuletzt: "Ich will dafür sorgen, dass das Budget weniger schlecht ist. Nicht, um es durchzuwinken - sondern um es ändern zu können, wenn ich Präsidentin bin."
Le Pen hat - ebenso wie die Regierung - ein Interesse daran, dass es bis Jahresende einen Haushalt gibt. Andernfalls müsste wieder ein "Spezialgesetz" her: eine Übergangslösung, durch die der Vorjahreshaushalt eins zu eins und zeitlich befristet ins neue Jahr gezogen werden kann. Es bietet aber keinen politischen Gestaltungsspielraum - und auch Sparmaßnahmen würden nicht direkt greifen.
Haushalt wohl nur mit riskanter Strategie realisierbar
Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu dürfte sich keine Illusionen machen: Den Sparhaushalt mit einer regulären Abstimmung durchs Parlament zu bekommen, scheint bereits jetzt unmöglich. Stattdessen könnte sich Lecornu erneut für Verfassungsartikel 49.3 entscheiden. Damit könnte er den Haushalt ohne Abstimmung durchs Parlament bringen - würde im Gegenzug aber Misstrauensvoten und den Sturz der Regierung riskieren.
Die wackeligen Mehrheiten im Parlament und der Profilierungszwang der Parteien vor der Wahl im kommenden Jahr machen den Haushalt für die Regierung einmal mehr zu einer politischen Quadratur des Kreises.

In Frankreich haben die Beratungen über den Haushalt begonnen. Angesichts hoher Schulden will Finanzminister Lescure deutlich sparen. Aber die Regierung hat keine eigene Mehrheit - und stößt auf Widerstand.
Der Rahmen wollte so gar nicht passen - gemessen an der politischen Bedeutung der Debatte. Zum Auftakt der Haushaltsberatungen stand Finanzminister Roland Lescure am späten Dienstagabend vor einem nahezu leeren Plenarsaal und versuchte die wenigen Anwesenden vom Ernst der Lage zu überzeugen: "2026 ist noch nicht vorbei - und das Jahr ist davon geprägt, dass sich Krisen häufen", sagte er. Man müsse unbedingt zu einem ausgeglichenen Haushalt zurückfinden. "Deshalb schlagen wir 2027 wieder den Sanierungskurs ein."
Finanziell steht Frankreich mit dem Rücken zur Wand: Die Schuldenquote liegt bei knapp 120 Prozent der Wirtschaftsleistung. Allein für Zinszahlungen auf Kredite sind im laufenden Haushalt fast 80 Milliarden Euro eingeplant.
"Wir dürfen uns damit nicht abfinden", mahnt Lescure. "Um zu verhindern, dass wir immer mehr Geld leihen müssen und um unsere Spielräume zu erhalten, gibt es nur einen Weg: unser Haushaltsdefizit zu reduzieren" - und zwar von aktuell 5,4 auf 5,0 Prozent der Wirtschaftsleistung.
Kürzungen in Höhe von 40 Milliarden Euro geplant
Dafür plant die Regierung in ihrem Haushaltsentwurf "Sanierungsmaßnahmen" in Höhe von gut 40 Milliarden Euro. Kürzen will sie bei Entwicklungshilfe und Beschäftigungspolitik, Renten und Wohnzuschüsse sollen nicht wie üblich an die Inflation angepasst werden.
Die Verteidigungsausgaben hingegen sollen deutlich steigen. Éric Coquerel von der linksradikalen Partei LFI ist Vorsitzender des Haushaltsausschusses. Er bezeichnete die Warnungen der Regierung als "Schwarzmalerei" und warf ihr vor, wirtschaftspolitisch gescheitert zu sein: "Diejenigen, die sagen, wir hätten kein Geld mehr, sind nicht in der Position, um Lektionen zu erteilen!"
Opposition sieht Scheitern der Regierung
Sie seien alle an ihren Versprechungen gescheitert, meint Coquerel: "Sie haben das Haushaltsdefizit nicht reduziert, die Arbeitslosigkeit steigt wieder und liegt bei gut acht Prozent." Diese Politik habe das Land kaputtgemacht.
Die Regierung steht vor einer fiskalischen Herkulesaufgabe. Und einem politischen Drahtseilakt. Denn in der Nationalversammlung hat sie keine eigene Mehrheit - und auf die Kompromissbereitschaft der Opposition kann sie wohl kaum zählen: ein halbes Jahr vor der Präsidentschaftswahl.
Sozialisten forderten Ablehnung noch vor Debatte
Im Laufe des Abends füllte sich der Plenarsaal in der Assemblée. Die Sozialisten hatten einen Antrag eingebracht, um den Budgetentwurf der Regierung abzulehnen, noch bevor die inhaltliche Debatte darüber überhaupt angefangen hatte.
Die Abgeordnete Estelle Mercier rechtfertigte den Schritt ihrer Fraktion: "Dieser Haushaltsentwurf zeichnet sich nicht durch Vernunft aus - sondern durch Ungerechtigkeit. Ein vernünftiges Haushaltsgesetz in einem Parlament ohne Mehrheit, in einem gespalteten Land müsste ein gerechtes sein. Es müsste eines sein, das alle an den Sparanstrengungen beteiligt, gemessen an ihren Fähigkeiten - und das dadurch kompromissfähig wäre."
Der Antrag scheiterte, die Budgetverhandlungen nehmen also ihren Lauf. Die Episode zeigt aber, wie groß der politische Druck auf die Regierung ist. Den letzten Haushalt konnte Regierungschef Sébastien Lecornu vor allem dank den Verhandlungen mit den Sozialisten durchs Parlament bringen - die jetzt aber auf Konfrontation gehen.
Le Pen denkt an ihre mögliche Präsidentschaft
Marine Le Pen verfolgt eine andere Strategie. Auf einer Veranstaltung von Politico sagte die Präsidentschaftskandidatin des rechtsnationalen Rassemblement National zuletzt: "Ich will dafür sorgen, dass das Budget weniger schlecht ist. Nicht, um es durchzuwinken - sondern um es ändern zu können, wenn ich Präsidentin bin."
Le Pen hat - ebenso wie die Regierung - ein Interesse daran, dass es bis Jahresende einen Haushalt gibt. Andernfalls müsste wieder ein "Spezialgesetz" her: eine Übergangslösung, durch die der Vorjahreshaushalt eins zu eins und zeitlich befristet ins neue Jahr gezogen werden kann. Es bietet aber keinen politischen Gestaltungsspielraum - und auch Sparmaßnahmen würden nicht direkt greifen.
Haushalt wohl nur mit riskanter Strategie realisierbar
Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu dürfte sich keine Illusionen machen: Den Sparhaushalt mit einer regulären Abstimmung durchs Parlament zu bekommen, scheint bereits jetzt unmöglich. Stattdessen könnte sich Lecornu erneut für Verfassungsartikel 49.3 entscheiden. Damit könnte er den Haushalt ohne Abstimmung durchs Parlament bringen - würde im Gegenzug aber Misstrauensvoten und den Sturz der Regierung riskieren.
Die wackeligen Mehrheiten im Parlament und der Profilierungszwang der Parteien vor der Wahl im kommenden Jahr machen den Haushalt für die Regierung einmal mehr zu einer politischen Quadratur des Kreises.

title: Росіяни вдарили по Дніпропетровщині: двоє загиблих, горять приватні будинки
content_c:
Росіяни вдарили по Дніпропетровщині: двоє загиблих, горять приватні будинки
Ворог зранку атакував громади Дніпропетровщини.
Уранці 15 жовтня російські війська атакували безпілотниками Дніпровський та Павлоградський райони Дніпропетровської області, внаслідок чого загинули двоє людей.
Про це повідомив голова Дніпропетровської обласної військової адміністрації Олександр Ганжа.
За його словами, внаслідок ворожої атаки в Новоолександрівській громаді зруйновано приватний будинок. Загинули двоє людей.
Також російські війська атакували Павлоград. Там зайнялися кілька приватних будинків.
На місці працюють рятувальники. Інформацію про можливих постраждалих у Павлограді наразі уточнюють.
Раніше повідомлялося, що у ніч проти 15 жовтня у Луцьку та Рівному пролунали вибухи на тлі атаки ворожих ударних безпілотників.
Ми раніше інформували, що у Луцьку рятувальники завершили пошукові роботи на місці кривавого російського удару по гуртівні товарів, який забрав життя 6 людей.

title: Украинские производители дронов зависят от китайских комплектующих, несмотря на локализацию — AP
content_c:
Украинские производители военных дронов по-прежнему в значительной степени зависят от китайской электроники и других критически важных компонентов. Это создает риск перебоев в производстве, если Пекин ограничит поставки или отдаст предпочтение российским заказчикам. Об этом сообщило информационное агентство Associated Press.
Украина стала одним из мировых лидеров в разработке военных беспилотников. Эти технологии помогают сдерживать значительно более многочисленного противника. Однако развитие дронов, которые существенно усилили боевые возможности Украины, выявило важную уязвимость. Их производители зависят от электроники из Китая — одного из ключевых союзников России.
Больше всего Украина опасается, что китайское правительство может существенно ограничить доступ к необходимым деталям. Еще один риск — китайские заводы могут отдавать предпочтение российским оборонным компаниям, которым требуются те же компоненты.
В течение последних двух лет Украина пыталась уменьшить эту зависимость. Она расширяла внутреннее производство и увеличивала закупки на Тайване, в Европе и США. Это сократило потребность в китайских электродвигателях, полетных контроллерах и других деталях.
Полностью отказаться от китайских поставок пока не удается. Поставщики из союзных стран не могут предложить столь же низкие цены и сопоставимые производственные мощности.
«Если Китай перестанет производить для нас… мы ослепнем. Это самое страшное», — заявил Андрей Таганский, один из руководителей украинского производителя вооружений Odd Systems, разрабатывающего камеры для дронов.
Китай уже несколько лет усиливает контроль за экспортом беспилотников и сопутствующего оборудования. Пекин объясняет это опасениями по поводу затягивания войны в Украине. Ограничения не остановили поступление китайских компонентов в Украину. Однако они привели к задержкам и увеличили расходы. Из-за этого украинские компании всё чаще обращаются к посредникам в третьих странах.
«У Китая есть рычаги влияния. Он может направлять больше материалов в Россию, одновременно ограничивая поставки на Запад», — отметил исследователь аналитического центра RUSI Роберт Толлост.
В Министерстве иностранных дел Китая заявили, что Пекин придерживается «взвешенного и ответственного» подхода к военному экспорту. Ведомство выступило против использования гражданских дронов в военных целях и призвало искать политическое урегулирование войны.
Украинская индустрия беспилотников завоевала международное признание благодаря передовым разработкам. Компании проектируют и собирают системы, которые изменили современную войну. В то же время производство многих материалов и компонентов для этих дронов не удастся быстро перенести в Украину. По словам представителей двенадцати украинских производителей, магниты, двигатели, микросхемы, тепловизионные датчики, аккумуляторные элементы и другие компоненты до сих пор в основном поступают из Китая.
Полный переход на западные аналоги может увеличить расходы до 60% и сократить производство примерно на столько же. Такую оценку привёл Александр Яковенко из крупной украинской оборонной компании TAF Industries. Несмотря на это, украинские производители уже постепенно снижают зависимость от Китая.
Развитие собственного производства имеет и дополнительное преимущество в условиях изнурительной войны. Украинские дроны и детали к ним можно переделать за несколько дней в соответствии с неотложными потребностями фронта. Внесение таких изменений через иностранные цепочки поставок может занимать месяцы, пояснил Артур Савчий, аналитик киевского Serpens Center for International Security.
В начале 2024 года почти 90% импортируемых Украиной деталей для дронов поступали непосредственно из Китая. За первые восемь месяцев 2026 года эта доля составила всего 28%, свидетельствуют данные украинской таможни. Однако снижение может быть менее существенным, чем кажется. Часть компонентов, которые учитываются как импорт из Польши или Чехии, скорее всего, были произведены в Китае и доставлены через эти страны.
Украина может собирать аккумуляторы, но элементы внутри них приходится импортировать. Для производства двигателей также требуются иностранные магниты и медь. Часть электроники украинские предприятия способны производить самостоятельно, однако китайские компании выпускают её в значительно больших объёмах и примерно вдвое дешевле.
Особенно заметна зависимость в производстве тепловизионных камер. Украинские компании самостоятельно разрабатывают эти камеры. В то же время они используют импортные датчики, улавливающие инфракрасное излучение, и линзы, которые не могут изготавливаться внутри страны. Одной из ключевых сырьевых составляющих является германий. Китай располагает им в больших объемах, поэтому китайские линзы значительно дешевле европейских аналогов.
США и европейские страны также производят датчики. Однако большую часть этой продукции они используют на своих рынках. По словам Таганского, Украина могла бы производить тепловизионные камеры полностью из европейских компонентов. Препятствиями остаются цена и ограниченные производственные мощности. Европа выпускает примерно 600 тысяч тепловизионных датчиков в год, тогда как потребность Украины он оценивает в 4 миллиона. Поэтому часть китайских деталей остается незаменимой.
По оценкам экспертов, Россия зависит от Китая ещё больше, чем Украина. Отчасти это связано с западными санкциями, которые ограничивают её доступ к другим рынкам. В то же время Москва не рискует оказаться в ситуации, когда её союзники в Пекине отдадут предпочтение украинским заказчикам. Конкуренция за заказы на тех же китайских заводах создаёт для Украины ещё одну опасность. Информация о её потребностях может стать известна противнику.
С 2023 года Китай несколько раз ужесточал экспортный контроль в отношении дронов и связанных с ними компонентов. Из-за этих ограничений украинские компании лишились возможности напрямую закупать у китайских производителей отдельные гражданские беспилотники большой дальности, двигатели, камеры и оборудование для инфракрасного изображения.
Напомним, что украинская компания TAF Industries подписала меморандум об оборонном сотрудничестве с люксембургской LUXUAV. Партнеры планируют развивать беспилотные технологии и производственные мощности в Бельгии и Люксембурге. Сотрудничество является частью инициативы Build with Ukraine, которая объединяет украинский боевой опыт с промышленными возможностями стран-партнеров.
Кроме того, литовская компания Unmanned Defense Systems открыла совместное предприятие UDS Ukraine для работы с украинскими военными и технологическими партнерами. Местная команда будет внедрять беспилотные системы, обучать операторов и поддерживать постоянное взаимодействие с подразделениями. Присутствие компании в Украине должно сократить время от определения потребностей военных до разработки и применения технических решений.
